title: Near-saturated observations retain transverse ambiguity and cannot validate a global source law
statement: For m3,a1 and readings F(+-e1)=+-(2+eps)e1,0<=eps<=2, inverse-zero transverse radius is exactly sqrt(eps*(2-eps)/8). At eps0 or2 it vanishes; for0<eps<2 it is positive and behaves like sqrt(eps)/2 near0. Bounded adversarial force bias separately prevents uniform inverse error below eps_noise/m. Finite compatible readings cannot establish the global shifted-sector contract.

contract.units: Saturation fixture uses normalized m3,a1,input length1; eps is its slope defect. eps_noise is a response-vector norm error; inverse floor has input units.

body: Two inverse balls have centers +-(1-3s/8)e1 and radius s/8,s=2+eps; averaging their squared inequalities gives radius^2=eps*(2-eps)/8. Adding the transverse endpoints satisfies all finite residual constraints, so the extension theorem realizes them in the global Lipschitz class, without a promised smooth physical realization. A noisy report phat_i with force error<=eps_i gives only outer radius b*||p-phat_i||+(b+c)*eps_i around x_i+c*(p-phat_i), not exact correlated-noise consistency. Fplus/minus=m*x+-eps_noise*e1 produce the identical reports m*x at every possible query and inverse separation2*eps_noise/m; this is an adversarial-bias floor, not an iid zero-mean noise theorem. A separate C3 hidden bump agrees with all retained readings yet violates monotonicity elsewhere, showing those readings cannot supply global validity. Do not round almost saturated reports into an exact forced inverse or treat a finite class check as a physical warranty.
